metadata.notes: Baseline for sift-email after question comments were replaced with (inferred) rubric lines (#137): when the rubric leaves a call open, sift takes the safe default and writes the call into the rubric as a dated (inferred) rule in the section for the priority applied; it opens and reads no comments. Evals 1-32, two runs each, with run-mcp-trials.sh against the Gmail, Claude Docs, and Contacts stubs, on SKILL.md as of commit 7b407a1, run in parallel with separate trial directories under $TMPDIR. Runs were on 2026-10-26 in the rubric timezone; fixtures are anchored to 2026-10-10 and shifted two weeks. Eval 21's 'no label for these categories outside AI/' check was overridden to pass in both runs, as in earlier rounds: the only such label left is the user's own seed label 'Newsletter', which sift must keep. Failures, all in run 1: eval 15 (moved the 22 Added by sift rules into Low priority word for word without consolidating them or trimming Examples, so three checks fail); eval 8 (added Examples lines about threads settled by the user's or Gmail's Important mark); eval 20 (left a PTA note under the soccer heading during the About me tidy); evals 28 and 32 (the user's first-person voice in a changelog entry copied from the rule or note it records). Not graded: eval 32 run 2 called the collection notice Junk, against When torn's 'Low priority over Junk'; some runs wrote (inferred) rules for calls the rubric already settled (evals 26 and 28 run 1); an (inferred) Tabs rule written as a bullet below the Tabs table (eval 22 run 2); About me placeholders replaced by sift's first note; Daily review lines duplicated or inline.
